prompt:
Approach this as a Statistical Physicist. Sees systems in terms of phase transitions, critical phenomena, energy landscapes, and attractors. Bring that lens to the problem.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Hysteresis loop mapping of AP-1 activity vs. stimulus
ideas.description: Ramp a controllable input (e.g., optogenetic or chemically induced ERK/JNK signaling, or inducible c-Fos/c-Jun) up and then down, and measure single-cell AP-1 reporter output and target-gene expression. A path-dependent loop, with different up and down thresholds that persist after the stimulus is removed, would indicate bistability. Memory would then be a property of the energy landscape rather than a lingering signal.

ideas.title: Bimodality and critical slowing down near the threshold
ideas.description: Tune stimulus dose or AP-1 abundance toward the putative tipping point and track single-cell time series with live reporters. Look for rising variance and autocorrelation time, diverging relaxation time after perturbation, and a shift from unimodal to bimodal distributions. These are generic signatures of a nearby bifurcation and would show whether AP-1 sits close to a transition.

ideas.title: Perturb-and-relax basin-of-attraction test
ideas.description: Deliver pulses of varying amplitude and duration, then knock AP-1 down transiently (degron, dominant-negative) or overexpress it, and record whether cells return to the original state or fall into a new one. Mapping the fraction of cells that settle in each state as a function of perturbation size gives the basin boundaries. Persistence after the perturbation is cleared, and its dependence on feedback loops such as FOS/JUN autoregulation, would separate attractor memory from slow decay.

ideas.title: Chromatin-state memory via time-resolved ATAC/CUT&Tag with AP-1 motif tracking
ideas.description: Profile accessibility, AP-1 occupancy and histone marks at AP-1-bound enhancers before, during and long after transient stimulation, including after cell divisions. Test whether enhancers opened by AP-1 stay open once AP-1 returns to baseline, and whether they enable faster or stronger re-induction. Pair this with AP-1 degradation at different times after the stimulus to separate initiation from maintenance of the memory.

ideas.title: Inference of a landscape and dynamical model from single-cell data
ideas.description: Combine single-cell RNA-seq or multiome data with live reporters to fit a stochastic dynamical model, such as a Langevin or Fokker-Planck model, of AP-1 and its targets. Estimate the effective potential, the number of minima, barrier heights and Kramers-type switching rates. Then test the predictions: the model should forecast how memory lifetime scales with noise, feedback strength and AP-1 dosage, and those predictions can be checked experimentally.
